newsitem.title: GERMANY: German tax talks break off without agreement.
newsitem.headline: German tax talks break off without agreement.

text.p: Negotiations between Germany's ruling coalition and opposition Social Democrats (SPD) broke off on Tuesday afternoon without an agreement on key tax reforms ahead of parliament's mediation committee meeting Wednesday.

Negotiators said there was no chance of reaching a deal on Finance Minister Theo Waigel's plan for sweeping cuts to income and corporate taxation, but there was still a chance of an agreement on abolishing a capital trading tax on companies.

Two days of meetings in working groups ahead of the committee meeting failed to resolve the differences which had led the SPD to vote down the government tax reforms in the Bundesrat upper house of parliament earlier this month.

"It is clear that we will not support the tax reforms in the mediation committee because we consider them unjust and anti-social," SPD parliamentary business manager Peter Struck told reporters after the talks.

Struck said he saw a chance of a deal on the capital trading tax, but said the SPD wanted to link that to cutting social insurance charges which are seen as inflating the cost of labour and destroying jobs in Germany.

Hans-Peter Repnik, tax negotiator for Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), also said there was a chance of a deal on the capital trading tax, but said he rejected SPD financing plans for the cuts in labour insurance charges.
